name: Reed Hastings
current_role: Co-founder of Netflix (left board in 2026 after serving as chairman); majority owner of Powder Mountain ski resort, Utah
profile: Co-founded Netflix in 1997 after selling his first company, Pure Software, and turned it from DVD-by-mail into the dominant streaming service. Stepped down as co-CEO in 2023, became executive chairman, and in April 2026 said he would leave Netflix's board. Now focused on Powder Mountain (bought control in 2023) and education philanthropy; lifetime giving above $2bn.
interesting_fact: Before college he deferred Bowdoin for a year to keep selling Rainbow vacuum cleaners door to door, a summer job he said he liked; he then taught math in the Peace Corps in Swaziland.
deep_cut_fact: He has put more than $100m of his own capital into Powder Mountain, Utah, and in 2026 announced a further $157m for its private Powder Haven area, adding two new lifts for the 2026-27 season. The resort also has an outdoor art museum.
notes: Leaving Netflix's board as of summer 2026, so Powder Mountain is the likelier route. The Netflix newsroom lists only regional press contacts, so none is a direct line to him. Ties to the podcast topics: education philanthropy and real estate/resort development.

name: Uma Devi Prasad
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2025-26) as a holder of Aristo Pharmaceuticals wealth; no executive role found
profile: Hurun links her to Aristo Pharmaceuticals, the Mumbai-based drugmaker founded in 1971 by Mahendra Prasad, a seven-term Rajya Sabha MP who died in December 2021. Public records name an Uma Devi in disputes over his estate. I could not confirm her role at the company or any public profile.
notes: Very private, with almost no public profile. Her link to Aristo is tied up in ongoing estate litigation over Mahendra Prasad's assets, so this is a sensitive family matter: avoid. The only contact is the company's general email. Low priority.

name: Lawrence Stroll
current_role: Executive Chairman and controlling shareholder, Aston Martin Lagonda; owner of the Aston Martin Aramco F1 team
profile: Montreal-born fashion investor who, with Silas Chou, built Tommy Hilfiger and then Michael Kors into global brands and cashed out after Kors' 2011 IPO. Bought the Force India F1 team in 2018, led a 2020 rescue investment in Aston Martin, and now runs both the carmaker and its F1 team (with Adrian Newey on board).
interesting_fact: He collects vintage Ferraris and paid a then-record $27.5m for a 1967 Ferrari 275 GTB/4*S N.A.R.T. Spider in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: He owned Quebec's historic Circuit Mont-Tremblant, a former Canadian Grand Prix venue, from 2000 until selling it in 2022. In 2021 he listed it for sale, then took it off the market.
notes: Gives few interviews. The best route is the Aston Martin corporate or F1 team press office (media.astonmartin.com).

name: Anthony Wood
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Roku Inc. (Fox agreed in June 2026 to acquire Roku; Wood is to join Fox's board at closing)
profile: British-born engineer (Texas A&M) and serial founder. He pioneered the DVR with ReplayTV, then founded Roku in 2002 and took it public in 2017; Roku is his sixth company. In June 2026 Fox agreed to buy Roku for about $22bn EV. Wood holds majority voting power and backs the deal, and will join Fox's board when it closes, expected in H1 2027.
interesting_fact: An early DVR innovator: before Roku he founded ReplayTV, one of the first digital video recorders, and sold it to SONICblue. He also sold website-builder iBand to Macromedia in 1996.
deep_cut_fact: His first sale was a single copy of software he wrote in high school, for $10. At Texas A&M he started SunRize Industries, which made digital audio tools for the Commodore Amiga, and later moved it to Silicon Valley.
notes: Timely angle: the Fox-Roku deal is pending, with closing expected in H1 2027. The press and IR emails are those listed in Roku's Q2 2026 release on Business Wire, as reported by search; I couldn't open the page to verify them directly. Older releases used ir@roku.com.

name: Ursula Hutter-Schleicher
current_role: Family shareholder in SCHWENK Zement (Ulm), per Forbes; no public operating role found
profile: Forbes says her fortune comes from SCHWENK, a family-owned Ulm building-materials group founded in 1847 that makes cement, concrete, sand and gravel and employs about 4,500 people. Her brother Eduard Schleicher, the fifth generation, runs the company. I found no public statements, interviews or a separate profile for her. She is not the late CSU politician Ursula Schleicher.
interesting_fact: SCHWENK is one of Germany's oldest family firms: Carl Schwenk founded it in Ulm in 1847, and the family has run it for five generations.
notes: Very private: only Forbes mentions her. The only route is the SCHWENK corporate contact (general company email), probably via the company's management, which her brother Eduard Schleicher leads. Cement links to the energy and decarbonisation angle.

name: D. Leopoldo Del Pino
current_role: Private investor and Ferrovial shareholder; former Ferrovial board member (until early 2016)
profile: Leopoldo del Pino y Calvo-Sotelo is a son of Rafael del Pino y Moreno, who founded Ferrovial in 1952, and inherited a stake in the infrastructure group. He sat on Ferrovial's board until early 2016 and has since gradually reduced his holding from over 8% to roughly 4%. His brother Rafael chairs Ferrovial. He invests privately, largely through SICAV vehicles.
interesting_fact: Ferrovial, the company his father founded in 1952, is now one of the world's largest infrastructure operators, with stakes in toll roads such as Toronto's 407 ETR and in Heathrow Airport.
notes: Very private, with no public role or published contact. He is not an executive at Ferrovial, so the company press office is not a real route to him. Press coverage centres on his SICAVs and stake sales. Low priority.

name: Robert Defares
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman/CEO, IMC Trading (IMC Financial Markets), Amsterdam
profile: Rob Defares co-founded IMC with René Schelvis in 1989 as a partnership of market makers on the floor of the Amsterdam Equity Options Exchange. IMC is now a global proprietary trading and market-making firm with about 2,000 employees across 10 offices. Defares has led it as CEO and chairman, sole CEO since co-CEO Wiet Pot left the board in 2017.
interesting_fact: IMC began as two traders on the Amsterdam options floor, where orders were made by hand signals, and became one of the first firms to build its own automated trading systems.
deep_cut_fact: The firm's original name was 'International Marketmaker's Combination', which is what the letters IMC stand for.
notes: Very low public profile: almost no interviews. The route is via IMC's Amsterdam office. IMC's data-centre and low-latency infrastructure fits the podcast's data-center angle. His current title (CEO vs chairman) comes from secondary sources, so verify it.

name: Luca Rovati
current_role: CEO of Fidim, the Rovati family office (Monza/Brianza); long-standing shareholder in Camfin, Pirelli's main holding company
profile: Son of Luigi Rovati, the pharmacologist who founded Rottapharm. Luca was Rottapharm's vice chairman and co-CEO until the family sold Rottapharm Madaus to Sweden's Meda in 2014 for about €2.27bn, then served as Meda's deputy chairman. With his brother Lucio he now runs the family office Fidim, which invests across biotech, pharma, real estate, hospitality and private equity.
interesting_fact: The 2014 Meda deal paid partly in shares and made the Rovati holding Fidim Meda's second-largest shareholder, with about 9%, until Mylan bought Meda in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: In late 2025 Fidim took a stake in Quantico Investment Club Opportunities, a club-deal platform that works exclusively with UniCredit. The Rovatis also sit alongside Marco Tronchetti Provera as long-time shareholders in Camfin, Pirelli's main holding company.
notes: Private family-office investor with no published press contact. The likely route is Fidim, the Rovati family office. The family also backs Rottapharm Biotech, run by his brother Lucio. Hurun last listed him in 2017.

name: Du Yinglian
current_role: Shareholder (about 3.5% directly) of Beijing Enlight Media (300251.SZ); acts in concert with her husband, founder Wang Changtian
profile: Du Yinglian is the wife of Wang Changtian, who founded and controls Enlight Media, one of China's largest private film studios. Hurun lists her wealth jointly with his. She holds about 3.5% of the company directly. Enlight's fortunes surged on the animated blockbuster Ne Zha 2 (2025). She keeps a low profile and has no public operating role.
interesting_fact: Enlight Media distributed Ne Zha 2 (2025), which became the highest-grossing animated film of all time worldwide and sent the studio's shares soaring.
notes: Private, with no public role. Any approach would go through Enlight Media's board secretary (Hou Jun) at the IR email listed in the company's annual report. Wang Changtian is the public face of the company.

name: Bom Kim
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chairman, Coupang, Inc. (NYSE: CPNG)
profile: Korean-American founder of Coupang, South Korea's dominant e-commerce company, built on Amazon-style rapid 'Rocket' delivery. A Harvard graduate and BCG alum, he founded a media company before starting Coupang in 2010. He took Coupang public on the NYSE in 2021, then the largest US listing by an Asian company since Alibaba. He runs the Delaware parent; Korean operations are led by local executives.
interesting_fact: He dropped out of Harvard Business School after about six months to start Coupang in 2010, shortly after selling his first company, Vintage Media.
deep_cut_fact: In 2004, a few years after graduating, he was planning a magazine for Harvard alumni and filed for trademark protection on the name '02138', Harvard's ZIP code. His memo said Harvard Magazine 'reads more like a collection of press releases and academic papers.'
notes: Rarely gives interviews. Coupang is under intense scrutiny in Korea after a large customer-data breach in late 2025, so expect a guarded PR team; lead with the logistics/automation angle. Route via press@coupang.com.

name: Michael Wu Po-kong
current_role: Former chairman and chief executive of Wing Lung Bank (Hong Kong); Secretary of the Wu Yee Sun Charitable Foundation
profile: The record mixes two people: the Chinese name 伍步高 is Dr Michael Wu Po-ko, while 'Po-kong' matches Patrick Wu Po-kong (伍步剛), Wing Lung's former vice chairman. Michael, son of bank founder Dr Wu Yee-sun, is a professional engineer who led Wing Lung Bank for more than 20 years until the Wu family sold it to China Merchants Bank in 2008. He is a prominent Hong Kong education philanthropist.
interesting_fact: His family's Wu Yee Sun Charitable Foundation pledged a major donation in 2007 that funded Wu Yee Sun College at the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
deep_cut_fact: He is a professional engineer by training rather than a career banker, and served as Treasurer of the Council and Court of Hong Kong Baptist University.
notes: Identity is ambiguous: the Chinese name 伍步高 points to Michael Wu Po-ko, but 'Po-kong' is his relative Patrick Wu Po-kong. Neither has been visible since the 2008 sale of the bank, and I could not confirm that they are alive. The family's philanthropy runs through the Wu Yee Sun and Wu Jieh Yee charitable foundations. No published contact; verify identity before any outreach.

name: Khalid Salim Bin Mahfouz
profile: Saudi banker and former chairman of National Commercial Bank. He died in Jeddah on 16 August 2009, aged 59. Same person as P03008 (Khalid Bin Mahfouz).
notes: Deceased in 2009; duplicate of P03008. Exclude.

name: William Hilton
current_role: Deceased (William Barron Hilton died 19 September 2019, aged 91)
profile: William Barron Hilton, former chairman and CEO of Hilton Hotels and founding owner of the AFL's Chargers, died on 19 September 2019 at 91. Most of his fortune was pledged to the Conrad N. Hilton Foundation.
